liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (1 review): Weir plays a distinctive little rhythm figure, audible around 3:08 when Garcia quiets, which shapes this whole performance [10]
- **Death Don't Have No Mercy** (1 other source): This tape's version of the song is cut [1]
- **Cryptical Envelopment** (1 other source): The tape's Cryptical Envelopment cuts in at the start of the first verse [1]
- **Jam** (1 other source): The jam is Garcia playing with the drummers [1]

## The recordings

- **gd68-09-02.sbd.volkerding.1979.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 14 songs; 70 min; rated 4.17/5 by 6 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the mix is poor: Weir is almost inaudible, vocals faint, and Phil is low [8]
- **gd68-09-02.sbd.miller.22095.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 11 songs; 108 min; rated 3.84/5 by 19 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the soundboard decent with good energy, but thinks some vocals should be louder in the mix; Reviewer describes the soundboard's sound as vivid and sharp; Reviewer calls the sound very clean, present and well balanced; alternate mixes of the whole show are included as bonuses [4][5][9][11][13][15]
- **gd1968-09-02.sbd.miller.115592.flac16**: soundboard; 12 songs; 104 min; rated 3.86/5 by 14 [2]

## Around the show

- The tape opens with an announcer introducing the band as the people who started it all, referencing yesterday [12]
- Pigpen makes odd humming or noises into the microphone at the start, according to the reviewer [15]
- Show contains all three major jams of the period: Other One suite, Dark Star through Death medley, and Alligator into Caution [9]
- Reviewer finds this Dark Star unique among those they know, with Weir more experimental in rhythm than late-1968 norm [10]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd68-09-02.sbd.volkerding.1979.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Pat Volkerding; source: Soundboard [1]
- **gd68-09-02.sbd.miller.22095.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Soundboard [3]
- **gd1968-09-02.sbd.miller.115592.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel (1/2-inch 4-track reels recorded on Ampex 440) -> Dat (Tascam DA30/44.1k) [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by talkfromtherockroom.com: [Put the Boot In: Grateful Dead- September 2, 1968 –Betty Nelson’s Organic Raspberry Farm | Talk From The Rock Room](https://talkfromtherockroom.com/2021/06/put-boot-in-grateful-dead-september-2.html) [17]
- Fan art by Jerry Garcia: [1968-09-02 Betty Nelson's Organic Raspberry Farm, Sultan, WA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1968-09-02-betty-nelsons-organic-raspberry-farm-sultan-wa-usa/) [18]
- Poster by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1968-09-02 Mon Labor Day Betty Nelson's Organic Raspberry Farm, Sultan, WA](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1405762212085/grateful-dead-1968-09-02-mon-labor-day) [19]
- Poster by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1968-09-02 Mon Labor Day Betty Nelson's Organic Raspberry Farm, Sultan, WA](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1405762212085/grateful-dead-1968-09-02-mon-labor-day) [20]
- Fan art by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1968-09-02 Mon Labor Day Betty Nelson's Organic Raspberry Farm, Sultan, WA](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1405762212085/grateful-dead-1968-09-02-mon-labor-day) [21]
